basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A value assertion about a subject and interest, distinct from the offer, transaction or invoice where money changes hands.
Separates observed prices from appraised values with stated basis, approach and assumptions.
Every value carries amount, unit, currency, effective date and uncertainty.
Price indices are structured aggregates of observations, not single prices.

may: Record observed prices with source, time, unit and currency.
Compute indicative values with the method and assumptions stated.
Convert currencies using a declared rate source and date.
mustNot: Present an indicative estimate as a formal appraisal or fair value.
Hide assumptions, comparables or uncertainty behind a single number.
Coordinate or signal prices with competitors.
Alter a recorded valuation instead of issuing a correction.
requiresHuman: Signing a valuation for lending, tax, accounting or legal use.
Choosing the basis of value for a regulated purpose.

considerations: Valuations affect taxes, loans, compensation and divorce settlements, so bias harms real people.
Algorithmic pricing can discriminate between customers or enable tacit collusion.
Price indices used for wages and benefits must be accurate and transparent.
affectedParties: Owners and buyers of the valued subject
Lenders, tax authorities and courts relying on values
Consumers affected by prices and indices

items: A value assertion has a subject, an amount with currency or unit, an effective date, a basis and a source or appraiser.
It is confused with a list price offer, an invoice amount and an accounting book value.
Losses from decisions on stale or mis-scaled values.
Unit or currency confusion between observations.
